descriptions.text: The Earning.Farm EFVault contract on Ethereum was vulnerable to reentrancy in its withdraw() function due to a logic flaw: the function transferred ETH to the caller before burning the corresponding ENF_ETHLEV share tokens, violating the Checks-Effects-Interactions pattern. Additionally, the inherited ERC20 methods lacked non-reentrant modifiers. The attacker used an 80,000 ETH flash loan to deposit ~320 ETH into the ENF_ETHLEV contract, then called withdraw(). Upon receiving the ETH callback — before the share balance was updated — the attacker re-entered the contract to override the share balance state and subsequently burned a small number of LP tokens to collect additional ETH. This cycle was repeated across nine transactions, extracting approximately 291 ETH (roughly $286K) from the protocol. Attack Tx: 0x6e6e556a5685980317cb2afdb628ed4a845b3cbd1c98bdaffd0561cb2c4790fa Analysis: How Was the Earning Farm Exploited? (Neptune Mutual)

The attack exploited both reentrancy and a flawed business logic in the share burning process, where withdrawals were processed before shares were burnt. Vulnerable Code Snippet: Attack Transaction: https://etherscan.io/tx/0x6e6e556a5685980317cb2afdb628ed4a845b3cbd1c98bdaffd0561cb2c4790fa Analysis: https://twitter.com/Phalcon_xyz/status/1689182459269644288

The DeFi project Earning.Farm suffered a reentrancy attack and lost 286 ETH (approximately $530,000). According to the analysis of SlowMist, the attacker re-enters the transfer function of LP to transfer LP tokens when withdrawing money, making the balance of the account smaller than the previously calculated shares value, triggering the logic of updating the shares value, resulting in the number of manipulated LPs being updated to the desired value. In terms of the value of the burned shares, this resulted in the final amount of LP burned being much smaller than expected, and the user can withdraw the funds in the pool by withdrawing the transferred LP again.

Earning Farm's EFVault on Ethereum was exploited on 2023-08-09 after a withdrawal callback let attacker-controlled code move ENF_ETHLEV shares before the burn step completed. Public estimates place the loss at roughly $528k to $541k. EFVault called IController(controller).withdraw(assets, receiver) before burning the caller's shares, so the receiver callback could change share ownership before accounting finished. The pre-call balance check did not protect the post-call burn.

Earning.Farm on Ethereum Mainnet was exploited on August 9, 2023, due to a reentrancy vulnerability in its withdrawal logic. The attacker drained over 291 ETH (approx. $540,000) by exploiting the ordering of external calls and share burns, enabling double withdrawals against the same share tokens. The EFVault contract violated the Checks-Effects-Interactions (CEI) pattern in its withdraw() function. ETH was transferred externally before shares were burned, allowing an attacker to reenter via a callback, transfer shares away, and repeatedly withdraw assets against the same shares.
